journal: The completed Aug. 13 tape was decisively constructive: the S&P 500 closed at a record 7,798.99, up 0.65%, the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.81%, and the Russell 2000 also reached a record. My independent calculations from completed daily bars put SPY 3.1% above its 20-day average and 10.3% above its 200-day average; equal-weight RSP rose 0.74% on the day and stood 2.7% above its 20-day average. That is a strong trend with participation beyond a single mega-cap lane.

The macro impulse improved at the margin. BLS index levels imply July headline CPI rose about 0.07% month over month while final-demand PPI slipped about 0.03%; the Treasury's official curve shows the 10-year yield fell to 4.63% from 4.68% and the 2-year to 4.15% from 4.20%. But this is not an all-clear: the same BLS levels imply roughly 3.30% year-over-year CPI and 4.66% year-over-year final-demand PPI, while the Fed's July 29 statement called inflation elevated and recorded three votes for a rate increase.

Bottom line: momentum, breadth, cooling monthly inflation, and lower yields outweigh the restraints, so I classify the market as Risk-on at 7.2/10. I stop short of higher conviction because long yields remain restrictive, calm volatility can hide fragility, and geopolitical or inflation shocks could rapidly reprice a richly trending market. This is market-wide research, not a recommendation to trade or size positions.

July CPI and final-demand PPI index levels were nearly flat month over month, while official 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields fell five basis points on Aug. 13.
what_holds_it_back: The official Treasury curve still ended Aug. 13 at 4.63% for 10 years and 5.21% for 30 years, restrictive discount rates for long-duration assets.
The Fed still described inflation as elevated on July 29, and three FOMC voters preferred a 25-basis-point rate increase.

Latest official Cboe history available during this assessment ended Aug. 12 with VIX at 14.55; very low volatility supports the tape but leaves little cushion if geopolitical or inflation news deteriorates.
what_changes_my_mind: I would upgrade if broad indexes keep making highs while equal-weight and small caps participate, credit remains firm, and inflation/yields continue easing without a growth shock.

I would downgrade on a sustained break below 50-day trends accompanied by wider credit spreads or a volatility surge, especially if renewed inflation pushes the 10-year yield materially above its recent range.

journal: Regular-session evidence is constructive. SPY closed at 772.49, up 0.25% on the day and 2.34% over 20 sessions; QQQ gained 0.73% and IWM gained 0.57%. The contradiction is valuation sensitivity to rates. Bottom line: risk-on, not carefree. Tight high-yield spreads and loose financial conditions support the tape, but low volatility, above-trend equity prices, and elevated long yields leave less room for macro disappointment. I would downgrade if volatility and credit begin confirming each other on the downside; I would upgrade if participation stays broad while yields retreat without a growth scare.
